name: Webwood Egg
summary: In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker seeks an unhatched Webwood Egg for his study of Teldrassil’s wildlife. After gathering venom samples, he needs a living specimen to examine the unnatural aggression afflicting the forest’s creatures. An egg can be studied safely without subduing a full-grown spider.

sections.title: A Safe Specimen
sections.body: Gilshalan Windwalker needs live subjects to understand the unnatural corruption affecting the Webwood spiders around Shadowglen. You have secured raw venom from the aggressive spiders, but carrying a thrashing giant out of the depths would be deadly for a novice. Gilshalan asks you to bring back an unhatched egg from the brooding clutches inside Shadowthread Cave.

sections.title: The Road to the Capital
sections.body: Webwood spiders brood in Shadowthread Cave, where the forest’s increasingly hostile arachnids make their nests. An intact egg gives scholars a controlled subject that can hatch under containment. Gilshalan plans to bundle it with his venom samples and send both to Darnassus for examination. With his local study complete, he directs recruits toward higher duties in the boughs of Aldrassil.

faq.q: Why does Gilshalan want an egg instead of an adult spider?
aliases: why not catch a live spider
faq.answer: Gilshalan wants an egg because capturing a live giant spider is too dangerous for an unproven recruit and too difficult for him to contain alone. Researchers can transport an intact egg safely and arrange containment before the brood emerges.

faq.q: Where is the Webwood egg found?
faq.answer: The egg lies in a webbed nest deep inside Shadowthread Cave, at the northern end of Shadowglen in Teldrassil, among the boughs and roots.
Gilshalan Windwalker is a night elf researcher stationed at Aldrassil in Shadowglen. He investigates the sudden corruption driving Teldrassil’s native creatures to violent behavior.

faq.q: What happens to the egg after it is turned in?
aliases: what does gilshalan do with the egg
faq.answer: Gilshalan prepares the egg and his venom vials for shipment to Darnassus. Scholars and druids there can examine them under controlled conditions after his work in Shadowglen concludes.

faq.q: What comes after completing this task?
faq.answer: After you secure the egg, Gilshalan directs you up Aldrassil to answer Tenaron's Summons and meet the elder druids guiding the heart of Shadowglen.

faq.q: Why are the Webwood spiders so aggressive?
faq.answer: The Webwood spiders, like much of Teldrassil’s wildlife, have been succumbing to unnatural corruption taking root across the young World Tree. It turns once-docile or neutral beasts into aggressive predators.

angles.text: For a young night elf, recovering the egg shows how corruption is taking hold on Teldrassil. Scholars now study their homeland’s wildlife as hostile threats.
As a druid, you know that Cenarion researchers study eggs and venom to learn whether the corruption altering these beasts can be cleansed or whether the blight runs deeper.
